data.title: Multi-modal tokenizers
data.summary: Per-modality tokenizer choice, codebook layout, token-id namespacing, persistence format — the interface world-model-v0 consumes.

alignment-12-4.rationale: Separate encoders + contrastive NT-Xent / InfoNCE for §12.4 multi-modal alignment. More expressive cross-modal structure than cosine on a shared projection; proven in CLIP/ALIGN. Accepted ~10–15% parameter overhead and the second training stage as the right trade-off for plasma + camera + magnetics alignment quality.

notes.body: Locked the 4 §12 decisions on tokenizers-12-landed; keeping the evergreen page's decision rows open so anyone reading the live doc sees what's in flight.
Drafted §12 expansion plan as 6 sub-items. Ranked by ROI; cross-modality alignment quality metric (§12.6) is the lowest-cost and worth landing first.
The Apache-2.0 constraint is non-negotiable. If Cosmos-Tokenizer-DV needs an NVIDIA OML license check, we're out — Option B becomes dead even if cheaper to ship.

q1 (§12.4 alignment metric) resolved 2026-05-26: per-modality InfoNCE chosen over cosine on shared embeddings. Decision alignment-12-4 locked. §13.1 scaffold dependency question (q2) remains open — see tokenizers.json#questions[q2].

questions.body: Should §12.4 use cosine on shared embeddings or per-modality InfoNCE? Need a 2-paragraph trade-off note before locking.
Does the §13.1 scaffold need to wait on §12.4 alignment improvements landing first, or are they independent?
